title: A Voice in the Night
overview: The LORD speaks for the first time to the boy Samuel, giving him a hard message about Eli's family, and Samuel grows up to be known across Israel as a true prophet.

parts.label: A quiet, dark time (v. 1)
parts.note: Samuel is serving at the sanctuary under the old priest Eli, whose own sons, the chapters before tell us, were corrupt. The verse says a word from the LORD was rare in those days and visions were few, which makes what follows stand out.

parts.label: Three calls, three mistakes (vv. 2-9)
parts.note: The sanctuary lamp burned through the night and was put out near dawn, so this happens in the early hours; some readers also see a hint that God's light had not yet gone out in Israel. Samuel has never had God speak to him, so he keeps running to Eli, until Eli realizes who is calling and teaches him how to answer.

parts.label: A heavy first message (vv. 10-14)
parts.note: Samuel's first word from God confirms an earlier warning against Eli's family, because Eli's sons treated God with contempt and Eli did not stop them. Saying no sacrifice will ever cover their guilt is pointed, since abusing the sacrifices was their very sin.

parts.label: Telling Eli the truth (vv. 15-18)
parts.note: Samuel is afraid to repeat the message, but Eli makes him tell everything by putting him under a solemn oath. Eli accepts it as the LORD's decision, and readers differ on whether that shows humble trust or tired resignation.

parts.label: Samuel becomes a known prophet (vv. 19-21)
parts.note: None of Samuel's words "fell to the ground," meaning what he said came true. People from Dan in the far north to Beersheba in the far south recognized him, and God kept speaking to him at Shiloh, where the sanctuary stood.

disagreement: Christians differ on whether this chapter is mainly a pattern for how God calls ordinary people today or mainly the account of a one-time turning point, when leadership in Israel passed from Eli's failing priestly family to Samuel.
think: Why might a hard truth be easier or harder to hear depending on who delivers it?
